mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
regime_hint: preemptive inflation surprise in a stable policy regime
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average by more than 0.5 percentage points, or inflation reverts below 0.3% within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index above the prior quarter's median signals wage pressure, which is associated with higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > median(PAYEMS, quarter prior) for two consecutive months
regime_hint: labor cost growth acceleration in a steady employment regime
failure_condition: Empirical power of the wage-cost signal falls below 0.05 (p-value) in out-of-sample tests, or 20-day forward returns remain negative despite persistent wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO manufacturing index below 50 triggers a supply-side shock that elevates risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 50 for a continuous 2-week period
failure_condition: No significant negative excess returns in 20 out of 25 identified supply shocks, or INDPRO recovers above 50 within 30 days in all cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST retail sales exceeding 2% above the prior month's level, occurring during a rising UNRATE labor market, predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Interaction IC < 0.05 in walk-forward tests, or 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero when both triggers are present.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in FEDFUNDS below 4% for three consecutive months signals accommodative policy, which elevates equity risk premiums and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 100 such episodes, 60-day forward returns do not exceed the mean by more than 0.8 percentage points, or FEDFUNDS re-enters the 4% band within 30 days in all cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% in a month with rising PAYEMS labor costs suggests disinflationary pressure, which reduces uncertainty and produces positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
regime_hint: labor market cooling with cost pressures
failure_condition: IC for the interaction is negative in out-of-sample tests, or 5-day returns are not statistically positive when both triggers occur.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip decline in INDPRO below 90 in two consecutive months indicates persistent supply-side weakness, which elevates volatility and yields negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant negative returns in 15 such double-dip episodes, or INDPRO recovers above 90 within 15 days in all cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in FEDFUNDS above 5% in a month coinciding with a decline in GDPC1 demand index below 110 signals tightening policy, which compresses discounting and produces negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% AND GDPC1 < 110 for the same month
regime_hint: policy tightening coinciding with soft demand
failure_condition: Interaction IC > 0.1 in walk-forward tests, or 60-day returns do not underperform baseline by more than 0.2 percentage points during such episodes.
